PatchCredentialRequest.description:
Either status (to archive) OR update fields (external_unique_id, expires_at). Mutually exclusive.
- If status is passed, other fields must not be passed (400).
- If status=archived and credential is already archived, returns 400.
- Only status=archived triggers archive; status=active is invalid for PATCH.
- If external_unique_id or expires_at are set, reuses update logic.

status.description: Set to "archived" to archive. Mutually exclusive with update fields.

external_unique_id.description: External unique identifier. Mutually exclusive with status.

expires_at.description: Expiration timestamp. Mutually exclusive with status.

PatchCredentialTypeRequest.description:
Either status (to archive) OR update fields (title, description). Mutually exclusive.
- If status is passed, other fields must not be passed (400).
- If status=archived and credential type is already archived, returns 400.
- Only status=archived triggers archive.
- If title or description are set, internally calls UpdateCredentialType (PUT).

post.description:
Registers a new policy implementation by supplying its name, description, on-chain addresses, and a policy_config_schema that declares the policy's configurable parameters.

The policy_config_schema is a JSON Schema document (draft-07) extended with ACE-specific fields:
- **properties** — one entry per configurable parameter (e.g. an allowlist or a threshold). Each entry requires type, description, and a metadata block.
- **metadata.on_chain_operations** — maps each type of config change (add, remove, replace) to a Solidity setter function. Copy the function_abi from your contract's JSON ABI build artifact.
- **policy_run_parameters** — transaction values extracted by the policy engine and passed to the contract's run() function at enforcement time. Use [] if none.
- **initial_configs** — ordered list of parameter names that must be set at deploy time (matching the configure() argument order). Use [] if none.
- **$schema**, **type**, **additionalProperties** — always the fixed values shown in the example below.

post.description: With `source` set to `list`, adds the addresses in `addresses` to the watchlist of your organization. With `source` set to `registry`, adds the active onchain addresses of the identities in the ACE identity registry `registry_id`; omit `addresses`. If an address is already on the watchlist, the request returns `409` and no address is added.

409.description: Duplicate monitored address

get.description: Returns the addresses on the watchlist. `monitored_address_trm_score` is `null` until the address is screened for the first time. After that, `last_screened_at` is the time of the latest screening and `risk_score_level` is the latest TRM risk level.

post.description: Registers exactly one primary contract (the monitored token) and zero or more associated contracts in a single request. `group_id` in the response is the `id` of the primary contract. The `func_abi` entries define the functions Active Monitoring can read and call: the signature and the read or write mode are derived from them. Each `chain_selector` needs a created CRE Connect Wallet for your organization. `active_rule_group` is `null` until you create a monitoring rule.

409.description: Duplicate title, function, or onchain deployment

get.description: Returns one item per primary contract. `active_rule_group` is the header of the active monitoring rule, or `null` when the token has none.
`contract_group_id` is the `id` of the primary contract. The `id` of an associated contract returns `404`. The response includes `active_rule_group`, or `null` when the token has no active rule.

Returns the named values you can use as `argument_mapping.value` when `mapping_type` is `reference`. `screened_address` is the screened address. `holder_balance` is the raw `balanceOf` value of the screened address on the primary token. System variables have a `null` `value`: Active Monitoring resolves them when it builds the call.

post.description: Creates the monitoring rule of a token. The rule is active immediately and cannot be edited: to change it, archive it and create a new one. `contract_group_id` is the `id` of the primary contract, which must not already have an active rule. `admin_function_id` must be a write function of its contract, and `argument_mapping` must contain exactly one entry per input of that function. Condition paths are `risk_level` for `trm_event` and `balance` for `read_balance_event`. A `reference` value is an action variable key, such as `screened_address` or `holder_balance`, or a path such as `trm_event.address`.

409.description: Contract already has an active rule group

get.description: Returns monitoring rules in the same shape as the get endpoint. Filter by `status` (`draft`, `active`, or `archived`) and by `contract_group_id`, the `id` of the primary contract. Filters combine.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by rule-group status. Omit to return all statuses.

parameters.name: contract_group_id
parameters.description: Primary contract instance id (group id). Same value as rule-group `contract_group_id`.

get.description: Returns the rule with its conditions and actions. Contracts and enforcement functions are expanded with their titles and ABI signatures.

patch.description: The only change allowed is archiving: set `status` to `archived`. An archived rule cannot be reactivated, and archiving it again returns `409`. Returns the same shape as the get endpoint.

409.description: Rule group is already archived

post.description: Stores the API key of the screening provider. The key is encrypted, never returned, and not validated when you store it. An organization has one key per provider: posting a key replaces the existing one.

201.description: Key stored (metadata only; the key is never echoed back)

get.description: Returns the status, the last four characters, and the timestamps of the stored key. The key itself is never returned. Returns `404` when no key is stored.

404.description: No key stored for this org and provider

delete.description: Removes the stored key. Active Monitoring stops screening until you store a new key.

post.description: Sets the number of hours between two screening runs. The change applies from the next scheduled run: a run that is already scheduled keeps its time.

get.summary: Get the org's TRM screening interval

200.description: Configured interval, plus whether a screening chain is currently active

404.description: No interval configured for this org

get.description: Returns the configured interval and `screening_active`, which is `true` while recurring screening is running. Returns `404` when no interval is configured.

delete.description: Removes the configured interval. There is no default interval. A scheduled run still executes once more, then screening stops until you set a new interval and call the start endpoint again. To stop immediately, use the stop endpoint.

post.description: Starts recurring screening. It requires a configured screening interval, a stored TRM API key, an active monitoring rule, and at least one address on the watchlist; otherwise it returns `400`. The first run starts immediately and repeats at the configured interval. Calling it while screening is running changes nothing.

202.description: First screening run enqueued, or a chain was already active for the org

400.description:
A precondition for starting screening isn't met yet: no screening interval
configured, no TRM API key configured, no active rule config, or no monitored
address.

post.description: Stops recurring screening without changing the configured interval. A run that is already executing finishes, and the endpoint returns `409`: retry after it completes. Calling it while screening is stopped changes nothing. Start screening again with the start endpoint.

202.description: Active screening job cancelled, or no chain was active for the org

409.description: A screening occurrence is currently running; retry after it completes

get.description: Returns the decisions of every active monitoring rule of your organization, one item per rule evaluated for a screening event on one network. A decision is listed once it has an outcome (`output`): evaluations in progress and evaluations where the rule did not match are not listed. `flag_for_review` and `silently_log` decisions have an empty `enforced_actions` array. In the list, `trm_event` payloads contain only `address` and `risk_level`; the get endpoint returns the full payload, including `raw_response`.

parameters.name: primary_token
parameters.description: Filter by rule group contract_instance_id (primary token).

parameters.name: onchain_action_status
parameters.description: Matches the latest status on an auto-enforced onchain action's activity_history.

parameters.name: trm_risk_level
parameters.description: Matches risk_level on a trm_event input event payload.

get.description: Returns the full decision, including the stored input events: the TRM result (`trm_event`, with `raw_response`) and the balance reading (`read_balance_event`). `decision_log_id` is the `id` returned by the list endpoint.

post.description: Resolves a decision whose outcome is `flagged_for_review`. The outcome becomes `user_ignored`, and the required `note` is recorded. Requires a signed-in user identity. Returns the full decision.

409.description: Run is not flagged for review

post.description: Resolves a decision whose outcome is `flagged_for_review` by submitting 1 to 10 operations. The outcome becomes `manual_enforced_onchain_action`. Each `contract_id` and `admin_function_id` pair can appear once, and every argument mapping must be a `constant`. All definitions are validated before any operation is submitted: if validation or submission fails, the decision stays flagged. Requires a signed-in user identity. Returns the full decision, with `enforced_actions` in request order.

409.description: Run is not flagged for review
